sections.label: Uncertain validity of electronic LPAs
sections.summary: About 87,000 electronic LPAs made between 14 November 2022 and 4 January 2024 have uncertain validity.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: For the approximately 87,000 electronic LPAs made between 14 November 2022 and 4 January 2024, there is some uncertainty as to whether the LPAs were validly made.

sections.label: Retroactive validation of affected LPAs
sections.summary: The Bill adds section 12B to the MCA to retroactively validate LPAs made between 14 November 2022 and 4 January 2024 using the online system.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: The Bill provides for the retroactive validation of the affected LPAs by introducing a new section 12B in the MCA.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: Specifically, subsections (1) and (2) provide that an LPA made between 14 November 2022 and 4 January 2024, both dates inclusive, using the online LPA system, is not invalid as a deed and not invalidly created by reason only that it was not made in compliance with section 12A(1)(a).

sections.label: Support for amendment Bill
sections.summary: The speaker moves and supports the amendment Bill to retroactively validate electronic LPAs certified from 14 November 2022 to 4 January 2024.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: With that, Mdm Deputy Speaker, I beg to move.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I support this amendment Bill, which is necessary to retroactively validate the electronic LPAs certified from 14 November 2022 to 4 January 2024.

sections.label: Notification of affected individuals
sections.summary: A question asks whether affected individuals will be notified of the retroactive validation, noting press reports of October 2023 feedback on the omitted sentence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Considering that 87,000 electronic LPAs are affected, will the affected individuals be notified and updated on this retroactive validation? : It was reported in the press that the Ministry had received feedback on the omitted sentence from a member of the public in October 2023.

sections.label: NEHR role and legal exposure
sections.summary: A question asks about the NEHR system's role in helping affected parties, noting about 87,000 LPA documents face potential legal challenge.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: What is the role of the National Electronic Health Record (NEHR) system in assisting the affected parties with retrieving and sharing the necessary information in a timely manner?

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: This Bill purports to remediate the omission in the electronic LPA documents, due to which approximately 87,000 LPA documents are exposed to potential legal challenge.

sections.label: Concerns over omitted LPA statement
sections.summary: Digital LPAs are welcomed, but the omitted statement raises concerns, and a question asks about legal implications for holders of LPAs missing the sentence.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The move towards digital LPAs is a welcomed step towards greater efficiency and accessibility.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: However, the recent discovery concerning the omission of a statement in electronic LPAs raises grave concerns.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: First, what would have been the legal implications for holders of LPA documents missing the required sentence?

sections.label: Court cases on e-LPAs
sections.summary: The passage asks whether any Court cases have challenged the validity of e-LPAs due to a missing clause.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Third, have there been any Court cases challenging the validity of e-LPAs, due to this missing clause?

sections.label: Retroactive validation of electronic LPAs
sections.summary: The amendment retroactively validates affected electronic LPAs made between 14 November 2022 and 4 January 2024.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: With this amendment to the Mental Capacity Act, the affected electronic LPAs, made between 14 November 2022 and 4 January 2024, will be retroactively validated.

sections.label: Bar on legal proceedings
sections.summary: Subsection (3) bars legal proceedings on or after 6 March 2024 over LPA validity due to forms not matching section 12A(1)(a).

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: Subsection (3) of the Bill provides that no legal proceedings may be instituted on or after 6 March 2024 over the validity of these LPAs by reason of the instruments or forms, used in the making of the LPA not being in accordance with section 12A(1)(a).

sections.label: Simplified deputyship application process
sections.summary: A deputyship application may use the simplified process if all relevant persons consent and it seeks specific orders under the Mental Capacity Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: A deputyship application may also be filed on the simplified process if all relevant persons to the individual who lacks mental capacity consent to the application and where the deputyship application is for specific orders under the Mental Capacity Act, such as to withdraw up to $80,000 of P’s monies, where P refers to the person who lacks mental capacity or other common orders such as to consent to medical treatment.

sections.label: LPA uptake and fee waiver
sections.summary: Close to 210,000 Singaporeans aged 50 and above have made an LPA, and the LPA Form 1 fee is waived for citizens till 31 March 2026.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: To date, close to 210,000 Singaporeans who are aged 50 and above, have made an LPA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: The LPA Form 1 application fee is currently waived for Singapore citizens till 31 March 2026.
